capabilities.description: Re-run a past decision with varied inputs to test sensitivity and validate the decision process.
capabilities.feedback_into_real_decisions: Sensitivity findings feed META: if small weight perturbations routinely flip selections, the decision was fragile — META flags the dimension for recalibration. Replay reports on high-stakes past decisions become regression tests: any future NBA version must reproduce-or-justify divergences on the replay corpus before promotion.

parameter_variations.option_set_delta: Optional add/remove options (e.g., 'what if we had considered X')
parameter_variations.weights_vector: Optional alternate NBA weights (e.g., candidate strategy under test)

capabilities.name: decision_replay

output.confidence: HIGH for process claims (exact recomputation); outcome claims not made by this capability

replay_report.regime_under_replay: act / act_verify / hold / do_not_act under varied parameters
replay_report.sensitivity: which parameter variation flipped (or nearly flipped) the selection; ranked

capabilities.simulation_method: Deterministic re-execution. Load the record's observation snapshot and option set, apply parameter variations, re-run the NBA-COMBINATION-V1 pure function (S_weighted, R_effective, S_final, gate, regime) exactly as specified. No stochasticity in the decision computation itself — replay is bit-reproducible given the same NBA version. Diff the replay selection against the original selection.

capabilities.description: Estimate what would have happened had an unchosen option been selected.
capabilities.feedback_into_real_decisions: Persistent positive regret for a decision class is signal to META that the NBA systematically undervalues that option class — candidate weight adjustment. Individual high-regret decisions become Adversary review targets (was the miss foreseeable?). Counterfactuals never directly change a past decision; they change future scoring.

input.counterfactual_option_id: An option from the record's option set that was NOT selected
input.estimation_method: proxy | analogue | model (V1: proxy and analogue only; model reserved for world-model layer)

capabilities.name: counterfactual_simulation

output.confidence: MEDIUM at best; LOW when proxy-only or analogue_count < 10. Every report states its method mix.

counterfactual_report.analogue_count: number of historical analogues used (0 if proxy-only)
counterfactual_report.method_provenance: which estimation paths contributed, with weights
counterfactual_report.realized_value_available: boolean — whether the selected option has a delayed realized-value label yet
counterfactual_report.regret_estimate: float, positive means the unchosen option looks better in hindsight

capabilities.simulation_method:
Three estimation paths, used in combination with explicit provenance:
1. PROXY: the option's recorded S_final at decision time is the NBA's own ex-ante value estimate. Cheap, always available, but circular (same function being evaluated).
2. ANALOGUE: k-nearest-neighbor over the decision log — find past decisions with similar observation state (cosine similarity over the observation vector) where a same-class option WAS selected and has a realized_value label; return the mean realized value with confidence interval. Requires realized-value labels; degrades gracefully to proxy-only when analogues are sparse.
3. MODEL: explicit world/outcome model. NOT AVAILABLE in V1 — the method slot exists in the schema so outputs stay forward-compatible, but any V1 output claiming method=model is a schema violation.
Counterfactual regret = estimated_value(counterfactual) - realized_or_estimated_value(selected).

capabilities.description: Backtest a candidate decision strategy against historical decision records — test months of decisions in minutes, with zero real-world risk.
capabilities.feedback_into_real_decisions: A strategy report with beats_baseline=true becomes a promotion candidate entering the 4-gate promotion path (NBA self-score → Adversary audit → shadow → canary). Divergence cases feed the Adversary's red-team queue. Negative results are equally valuable: they are recorded as falsified strategies so META never re-proposes them.

candidate_strategy.nba_version: must be a released NBA version (no unreleased functions in backtest)

test_corpus.record_ids: or corpus query (e.g., all decisions in lane X since date Y)
test_corpus.validation_split: 30% held out, never seen during tuning

capabilities.name: strategy_testing

output.confidence: HIGH for process metrics (exact); MEDIUM for value claims (proxy-dependent where labels are sparse)

strategy_report.applicability_envelope: the decision classes and state-space region covered by the test corpus — the strategy is ONLY validated inside this envelope
strategy_report.divergence_cases: records where candidate and baseline disagreed most, for Adversary review

capabilities.simulation_method: For each record in the corpus: recompute the NBA selection under the candidate strategy (deterministic, exact). Compare candidate selection vs original selection. Score each recomputed decision by: (a) realized value of the selected option where labels exist, else (b) the option's S_final under the ORIGINAL weights as a neutral proxy (avoids letting the candidate grade its own homework). Aggregate over discovery split for tuning; report final metrics on the validation split ONLY. Metrics: selection-agreement rate, mean value delta vs baseline, win/loss/tie counts, per-decision-class breakdown, confidence intervals via bootstrap. A strategy that cannot beat baseline on the held-out split with p < 0.05 is rejected — no promotion candidacy.

capabilities.description: Mine the decision log for recurring patterns: what predicts realized value, where regret concentrates, whether thresholds are well-calibrated.
capabilities.feedback_into_real_decisions: Pattern reports are META's primary training signal: dimension correlations drive weight recalibration proposals, threshold findings drive threshold reviews, bias findings drive scoring-guidance updates. Every finding must survive a strategy_testing validation before it changes anything real — discovery proposes, backtesting disposes.

input.corpus_query: decision records filter (time range, lane, seat, decision class)

capabilities.name: pattern_discovery

output.confidence: MEDIUM; varies with label coverage. Findings from sparse labels are flagged as hypotheses, not conclusions.

pattern_report.findings: array of {pattern, effect_size, confidence_interval, n, decision_classes_affected}
pattern_report.recommended_validations: strategy_testing runs that would confirm or falsify each finding
pattern_report.threshold_recommendations: suggested threshold adjustments with supporting evidence (advisory only — thresholds change via governance)

capabilities.simulation_method:
Aggregate analytics over decision records with realized-value labels:
- dimension_value_correlation: Pearson/Spearman correlation of each scored dimension against realized value. A dimension with ~zero correlation is dead weight; a dimension negatively correlated is actively harmful.
- regret_by_class: mean counterfactual regret grouped by decision class — finds the classes where NBA chooses worst.
- threshold_calibration: for decisions near each threshold boundary (within 0.05), compare realized outcomes of ACT vs HOLD — are the 0.70/0.55/0.40 cutoffs placed where the value actually changes?
- bias_detection: systematic over/under-scoring, e.g., urgency scores consistently higher than realized urgency warrants.
- weight_sensitivity: which weight perturbations would have most improved historical realized value (constrained optimization on the log — the empirical counterpart to replay sensitivity).
All analyses require minimum sample sizes and report effect sizes with confidence intervals. Correlation is not causation — every pattern report carries that warning and a recommended validation (usually: a strategy_testing run).

decision_log_v1_record.description: The atomic unit Dream operates on. Every autonomous decision — including HOLD and DO_NOT_ACT — must emit one.
decision_log_v1_record.immutability: Append-only. Corrections are new records referencing the original, never edits.
required_fields: observation: structured state snapshot (the observation vector the decision was made on)
options: full option set, each with id, description, 10 dimension scores, risk score
per-option computed scores: S_weighted, R_effective, S_final
selected_option_id (null for do_not_act, with the leading candidate noted)
execution_receipt_id (null until executed; holds/do-not-acts never get one — that absence is data)
realized_value: {estimate, measured_at, measurement_method, confidence} — nullable; filled by delayed attribution

realized_value_attribution.minimum_label_density: Strategy_testing corpora require >= 20 realized labels and labels on >= 30% of acted records, else the corpus is rejected for promotion-candidate backtests (still usable for exploratory analysis, flagged as such).
realized_value_attribution.problem: A decision's true value is often knowable only later. Without delayed labels, Dream can only optimize proxies.
realized_value_attribution.protocol: Each acted decision carries a value-attribution plan at decision time: what observable would confirm value, by when, measured how. A scheduled attribution pass fills realized_value labels. Unlabeled decisions age out of strategy_testing corpora after the attribution window closes (they remain usable for replay and pattern discovery with flags).

replay_depth.cold_start_bootstrap: Pre-v1 history (board receipts, PR records, scorecard receipts) may be converted to partial decision records by a bootstrap converter. Converted records carry provenance=RECONSTRUCTED and confidence caps: usable for pattern_discovery hypotheses and replay exploration, NEVER for promotion-candidate strategy_testing corpora.
replay_depth.full_fidelity_from: Adoption date of decision-log-v1. Records before this date lack the structured fields Dream needs.
replay_depth.minimum_viable_history: Dream becomes useful for replay immediately (single records). Strategy_testing needs ~50+ full records; pattern_discovery needs ~100+ with label coverage. Until then, Dream operates in exploratory mode and says so on every output.

epistemic_boundary: V1 Dream simulates DECISION PROCESSES, not world outcomes. The NBA combination function is deterministic and pure, so replay and backtesting re-compute exact selections under varied parameters — that part is exact. Counterfactual OUTCOMES (what would have happened) are estimates via proxies and historical analogues, never facts. This boundary is explicit in every Dream output: process-simulation results carry confidence HIGH; outcome-estimation results carry confidence with method provenance and intervals. A future world-model layer may raise outcome confidence; V1 does not claim it.

epistemic_state.falsifier: If strategies that beat baseline in held-out backtests consistently fail to improve realized value through shadow and canary phases, the outcome-proxy methodology is invalid and Dream's promotion path must be suspended pending redesign. Dream would remain useful for replay and pattern discovery but not for strategy promotion.
epistemic_state.note: V1 is a process simulator with honest outcome-estimation boundaries. It is designed to be wrong in known, bounded ways — and to say so on every output.

adversary.adversary_audits_dream: Gate 2 of the promotion path. The Adversary audits strategy reports, backtest methodology, corpus construction, and applicability envelopes. Veto is binding.
adversary.dream_serves_adversary: Dream generates adversarial scenarios on request: worst-case historical subsequences, synthetic stress corpora (within the honesty constraints — synthetic scenarios are labeled SYNTHETIC and never enter promotion corpora), and sensitivity analyses the Adversary uses to probe a live strategy's fragility.
adversary.shared_invariant: Neither Dream nor Adversary can promote a strategy alone. Dream proposes with evidence; Adversary audits with suspicion; only the full 4-gate chain confers authority.

meta.dream_as_experiment_runner: META proposes heuristic changes (weight adjustments, threshold moves, new tie-breakers); Dream backtests them via strategy_testing and returns the strategy reports. This is the core recursive-improvement loop: META thinks, Dream tests, evidence returns.
meta.meta_governs_dream_budget: Dream compute is not free. META allocates the Dream experiment budget across competing hypotheses by expected information value — the most uncertain, highest-leverage questions get simulated first.
meta.pattern_reports_as_training_signal: Pattern_discovery outputs (dimension correlations, threshold calibration, bias findings) are META's training data for recalibration proposals. Every META proposal must cite the Dream evidence it rests on.

dream_to_nba: Promotion-candidate strategies enter NBA option generation as candidate policies (with provenance=DREAM and the full receipt chain attached).
Counterfactual 'consider option X' suggestions may be injected as additional options in live decisions, scored normally by NBA — Dream proposes, NBA disposes.
Applicability envelopes are checked by NBA before applying any Dream-promoted strategy to a live decision; envelope mismatch falls back to the baseline strategy and logs the mismatch.
nba_to_dream: Every NBA decision emits a decision-log-v1 record — this is Dream's fuel.

Live decisions may request an async 'dream check' (quick counterfactual on the top-2 options) before acting. The check is best-effort and timeout-bounded (default 30s); NBA never blocks on Dream. A missing dream check is not a failure.

mission: Maximum Verified Human Value per Moment, constrained by Proof, Provenance, and Continuity.
open_refinements: World-model layer: explicit outcome models would raise counterfactual confidence from MEDIUM to HIGH. This is the single biggest future upgrade and must itself pass Adversary audit before its outputs enter promotion corpora.
Synthetic scenario generation: governed synthesis of edge-case decision scenarios (labeled SYNTHETIC, quarantined from promotion corpora) for Adversary stress-testing.
Cross-seat federated Dream: seats share anonymized decision corpora for larger backtest samples without sharing raw observations.
Compute budgeting: formal cost model for Dream experiments; META's allocation policy as machine spec.
Urgency×evidence interaction: the known failure mode (urgent unverifiable claims) deserves a dedicated Dream analysis track.
principle: remember → simulate → compare → select → execute → verify → learn
rationale: The highest-leverage fact about Dream: the NBA decision function is deterministic and pure, which makes decision-process simulation EXACT. Most 'AI simulation' efforts drown in stochastic world-modeling; Dream V1 sidesteps that entirely by simulating the decider, not the world. Backtesting a candidate weight vector against six months of decisions is not an approximation — it is the literal recomputation of what the system would have chosen. That exactness is what makes Dream safe to trust for process questions. The honest boundary — counterfactual outcomes are estimates, never facts — is load-bearing: it prevents the plausible-but-wrong failure mode at the architectural level rather than relying on every consumer to remember the caveat. The 4-gate promotion path exists because a simulator that cannot promote its findings is a toy, and a simulator that promotes without gates is a hazard. Shadow-then-canary with automatic rollback means Dream's boldest discoveries can be tried with bounded blast radius. Finally, making Dream META's experiment runner closes the recursive loop: the system doesn't just learn from reality (slow, expensive, sometimes irreversible) — it learns from simulated reality first, and only pays the real-world tuition for strategies that survived Dream, the Adversary, the shadow, and the canary.

offline_guarantee.audit: Every Dream run logs its input corpus hash, strategy version, and output hash to the dream-results store. An independent verifier can re-run any Dream computation bit-reproducibly from the logged inputs.
mechanisms: Separate service identity with ZERO grants on production state stores, production APIs, and deployment pipelines. Dream's credentials cannot write to production even if its code tried.
Read-only mount of the decision log, which is an immutable append-only store — Dream cannot alter history, only read it.
No network egress from the Dream runtime to production endpoints (enforced at the infrastructure layer, not in application code).
All Dream outputs write ONLY to the dream-results store, a separate namespace invisible to production readers.
CI invariant: dream code paths may not import production-write clients. A static check fails the build if they do.
offline_guarantee.principle: Dream can read the past; it cannot touch the present. Structural enforcement, not convention.

gates.name: nba_self_score
gates.rule: Adopting the Dream-discovered strategy must itself score as the highest-value action under the current NBA combination function, evaluated as a candidate option with full dimension scoring. A strategy that cannot win the decision to adopt it is not adopted.

gates.name: adversary_audit
gates.rule: The Permanent Adversary audits the strategy report and methodology: overfitting checks (held-out discipline honored?), distribution-shift checks (is the future likely to resemble the corpus?), reward-hacking checks (does the strategy game the proxy metric?), applicability-envelope checks (is the envelope honestly drawn?). Adversary veto is binding — a vetoed strategy returns to Dream with the audit findings, never to production.

gates.name: shadow_deployment
gates.rule: The candidate strategy runs alongside live NBA decisions with ZERO authority for a minimum of M decisions (M=100 default, higher for high-stakes lanes). Every divergence between shadow and live selections is logged with both S_final computations. Shadow results must confirm or improve on the backtest before proceeding.

gates.name: canary_deployment
gates.rule: Limited production authority on a low-risk lane with tightened thresholds (act threshold raised by 0.05) and mandatory extra verification on every action. Realized values are tracked against the backtest predictions. Any statistically significant degradation vs baseline triggers automatic rollback to the previous strategy — no human decision required to roll back, human notification required after.

promotion_path.principle: No Dream output reaches production authority without passing all four gates. Each gate emits a receipt.
promotion_path.receipts: Each gate emits a signed receipt (gate name, strategy version hash, corpus hash, decision, timestamp, reviewer identity for gate 2). The full receipt chain is the strategy's provenance; a strategy without a complete chain has no production authority.

wrong_strategy_prevention.principle: Dream is an optimism engine; the safety stack assumes its outputs are guilty until proven innocent.

threats_and_countermeasures.countermeasure: Mandatory discovery/validation split; beats_baseline must hold on the HELD-OUT split with p < 0.05. Adversary explicitly tests for overfit signatures (high discovery delta, flat validation delta).
threats_and_countermeasures.threat: overfitting — the strategy memorizes the corpus instead of learning transferable policy

threats_and_countermeasures.countermeasure: Applicability envelope is mandatory output; NBA checks envelope match before applying a strategy to a live decision. Strategies carry an expiry: revalidation required after N decisions or T days, whichever comes first. Envelope violations are logged as Adversary findings.
threats_and_countermeasures.threat: distribution_shift — the future differs from the historical corpus (new lanes, new decision classes, regime change)

threats_and_countermeasures.countermeasure: Backtest scoring prefers realized-value labels over proxy scores wherever labels exist; minimum label counts are enforced. Adversary's reward-hacking check specifically hunts proxy exploitation. Post-promotion realized-value tracking with automatic rollback is the final backstop.
threats_and_countermeasures.threat: proxy_gaming — the strategy optimizes the S_final proxy rather than realized human value (Goodhart)

threats_and_countermeasures.countermeasure: Decision-log-v1 REQUIRES logging all four regimes including holds and do-not-acts with their option sets. Corpus queries must include non-acted decisions; a corpus skewed >90% to acted decisions is rejected for strategy_testing.
threats_and_countermeasures.threat: survivorship_bias — the decision log over-represents decisions that were acted on; holds and do-not-acts are under-logged

threats_and_countermeasures.countermeasure: Narratives are not evidence. Only the held-out numbers, the Adversary audit, and the shadow/canary results count. The pattern_discovery capability is required to produce a mechanism hypothesis, but the hypothesis never substitutes for the validation gates.
threats_and_countermeasures.threat: plausible_narrative — a strategy that backtests well by coincidence and tells a convincing story
